selection: round-robin strata by provider family and nativeForm; sha256 rank

samples.rationale: The pinned schema requires TransitGatewayId and models a transit-gateway multicast domain; transit networking and multicast are beyond the scoped VM network, subnet, firewall, and ingress path.

Certificates plus required ListenerArn make this a separately managed certificate assignment on an existing listener, semantically subordinate to neutral.load-balancer-listener rather than a new VM-connected resource concept.

The pinned schema requires one or more IAM Roles in an instance profile; this is the provider object attached to a VM to confer workload permissions, an important identity relation absent from the 19 concepts.

AddressFamily and PrefixListName identify a reusable set whose Entries hold network prefixes; it is an important referenced address-set abstraction distinct from an individual neutral.network-filter-rule.
Required Conditions, Actions, and Priority define application-layer listener routing behavior; the current neutral model and scoped load-balancer concept are network-load-balancing oriented.
The schema binds a multicast group address and network interface to a transit-gateway multicast domain; multicast transit-network membership is outside the scoped VM topology.
The S3-backed CA certificate bundle is a mutual-TLS trust configuration for a load balancer, not a basic VM-connected IaaS resource required by the scoped network-load-balancer model.
The two required identifiers associate a local-gateway route table with a virtual-interface group; hybrid/local gateway connectivity is outside the scoped VM deployment topology.
RevocationContents and TrustStoreArn manage certificate revocation within an mTLS trust store, a security detail outside the basic load-balancer and VM IaaS scope.
The required network interface, mirror target, and mirror filter compose packet mirroring for inspection or observability; traffic capture is outside deployment connectivity and filtering scope.
This resource selects a mirror destination by network interface, NLB, or gateway-load-balancer endpoint; it supports packet mirroring, which is outside the scoped VM topology.

Required VpcId makes this a VPC-scoped traffic-filter policy container; that meaning is already covered by neutral.network-security-policy-group, although AWS attaches this variant at subnet boundaries rather than directly to compute connectivity.
The schema associates a Client VPN endpoint with a subnet target network; VPN is explicitly outside the scoped Docker-on-VM deployment topology.
Required TransitGatewayId identifies a routing table within a transit gateway; multi-network transit routing is beyond the scoped single-VM-network topology.

The standalone internet gateway supplies the public-network edge used by VPC routing; no current concept represents this important public ingress/egress gateway even though public VM and load-balancer reachability depend on it.
TransitGatewayAttachmentId plus connect-peer configuration model a GRE/BGP transit-gateway peer; hybrid transit connectivity is outside the scoped VM deployment topology.
DestinationCidrBlock and ClientVpnEndpointId define a route for a Client VPN endpoint; VPN routing is explicitly outside the scoped topology.

SubnetId, connectivity type, and public/private address allocation properties identify a managed NAT egress gateway; this is an important private-subnet-to-external-network path absent from the current 19 concepts.
